title: ERP-WMS stock reconciliation mismatch resolution
content: Timing differences between ERP cutoff and WMS receipt processing cause recurring £1m+ gaps. Root cause: WMS receives goods 1-3 days after ERP records inbound PO. Solution: move WMS cutoff to match ERP close window.

title: WMS duplicate task creation after replenishment - patch 9.2.7
content: Known issue in WMS 9.2: duplicate replenishment tasks created if system receives two PO receipts in <5 second window. Fixed in patch 9.2.7. Workaround: increase event queue timeout from 1s to 5s in config.

title: Supplier rebate revenue recognition under IAS 18
content: Q&A on supplier rebate accounting: Rebates that depend on annual volume milestones are contingent revenues. Recognition: Accrue only when achievement is probable (>75% confidence based on forecast). Documentation: Get written rebate agreement from supplier, track volumes monthly, reconcile accrual quarterly. Auditor challenge points: Is forecast reliable? Is rebate terms clear? Test: Compare 3-year actual rebates to accrued amounts.

title: WMS integration setup: EDI vs API vs file transfer
content: 3PL integration options: EDI (proven, slow setup, LFTP/SFTP batch): 4-6 week setup, ~£5k/year. Risks: latency (2-4 hours), manual reconciliation. API (fast, requires dev resources): 2-3 week setup, ~£15k initial + £10k/year. Risks: downtime on vendor side. File transfer (simple CSV, risky): 1 week setup, <£2k/year. Risks: data loss if file corrupted. RECOMMENDATION: EDI for mature 3PLs, API for modern providers.

title: Moulded-pulp tray drop-test failures: ribbing vs wall thickness
content: Test results: Standard wall (2mm) + ribbing failed at 80cm drop. Root cause: ribbing concentrates stress at rib base. Fix A: Increase wall to 2.5mm (cost +£0.08/unit, weight +5%). Fix B: Add horizontal reinforcement ribs perpendicular to load (cost +£0.04/unit, weight neutral). Testing shows Fix B passes 120cm drops. RECOMMENDATION: Use Fix B. Impact: packaging NRV risk avoided.

title: Zip strength failures in apparel: seam selection and QC
content: Zip pull strength spec: 50N minimum (ISO 13441). Failures at 48N (4% under spec). Analysis: Two root causes - (1) Supplier using lower-grade brass slider (mechanical issue), (2) seam allowance too tight (construction issue). Field complaint data: 2.1% complaint rate on this SKU vs 0.3% average. Cost of remediation: New supplier tested = £0.12/zip. Solution: Switch supplier for this SKU only. Implement 100% peel test at pack stage.

title: Stock reconciliation process: timing and measurement differences
content: Common gaps between Operations (WMS) and Finance (GL) inventory balances: 1. Timing: WMS records receipt 2-3 days before GL (in-transit goods still counted as supplier's). 2. Status mapping: WMS 'reserved' ≠ GL 'available'. 3. Damage: WMS marks damaged same day; GL waits for write-off approval (lag = 5-15 days). 4. Cutoff: Month-end variance typically £500k-£1.5m. PROCESS: Finance reconciles monthly using GL cutoff date, not WMS date.

title: Store shrink control cost-benefit analysis
content: Shrink control ROI study (50 stores, 12 months): Tagging (RFID + EAS): Cost £18k setup + £2k/year. Shrink reduction: 0.8% → 0.5% (annual saving £120k). Payback: 2 months. Layout optimization (clear sightlines, lower shelves): Cost £8k one-time. Shrink: 0.8% → 0.65% (saving £45k). Payback: 2 months. Staffing (add Loss Prevention officer): Cost £35k/year salary. Shrink: 0.8% → 0.55% (saving £75k). Payback: 7 months. Recommendation: COMBINE tagging + layout for fastest ROI.

title: Nearshore sourcing in Morocco: lead time and cost benchmarks
content: Morocco vs Turkey comparison: Lead time: Morocco 8-12 weeks (consistent), Turkey 6-10 weeks (variable). Cost: Morocco 15-20% premium vs Asia, Turkey 10-15% premium. Strengths: Morocco - EU trade preferences, EU quality standards, language (French/Arabic/English). Turkey - established supply base, competitive pricing, fast logistics. Risks: Morocco - newer supply base, fewer alt suppliers; Turkey - geopolitical (Syria/Iraq proximity). RECOMMENDATION: Morocco for EU-only collections (EU preferential rates). Turkey for faster turnaround on reorders.

title: WMS patch 9.2.7 release notes and testing
content: WMS 9.2.7 patch summary: Fixes duplicate task issue (seen in v9.2.0-9.2.6). Also includes 3 minor fixes to batch picking, 1 security patch. Changes to queue timeout logic (default 5s now, was 1s). Test scope before deploying: (1) Run full PO receipt test (50 concurrent receipts), verify no duplicates. (2) Batch picking with 1000+ item picks, verify performance <2s per pick. (3) User access - verify no permission regression. Deployment window: Saturday 2am-6am recommended (4-hour window).
